Monitoring: Apocheima moth start to attack walnuts when buds sprout, before flowering.
When larvae become 1 cm long they start feeding from leaf edges.
Later appear about 1 cm diameter holes.
When larvae are 3 to 4 cm long, they eat entire leaves and leaf rips remain.
They feed all soft and fresh leaves and they will go to the next trees by spinning silk in mid- March.
Timing of action is immediately when first- instar larva (0.1 -1 cm) or second-instar larva (1-2cm) take 80~85% in all of larvae found.
Threshold of action is at 2-3 young larvae (2-3 instar, 1 to 2.5 cm) in each 50 cm branch of a tree.
